references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus asks the same question: "With whom shall I compare this generation?" Matthew uses almost identical wording to liken this generation to children in the marketplace.

The immediate continuation of Jesus' parable where he elaborates on the comparison with children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another, illustrating this generation's rejection of both John and the Son of Man.
Jesus uses similar language with the question "What is the kingdom of God like, and what shall I compare it to?" (τίνι ὁμοιώσω) — the same rhetorical question form used to introduce a parable.
Yet another example where Jesus asks "What shall I compare the kingdom of God to?" — showing Jesus' repeated use of this rhetorical formula to introduce parables.
The parallel text in Matthew that elaborates on the parable about the children in the marketplace and Jesus' conclusion that wisdom is justified by her deeds.
God asks rhetorically whom he can be compared with — a similar pattern using ὁμοιώσω (whom shall I compare), which Jesus adopts to introduce his parable.
Jesus refers to "this generation" (τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης) as evil and faithless, the same expression found in Luke 7:31, showing that this generation rejects God's messengers.
Jesus speaks of "this generation" with a deep sigh, pointing to its unbelief and demand for signs — the same theme of a generation rejecting God's envoys.
